newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin renames Revolution Day "Day of Accord".
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin renames Revolution Day "Day of Accord".

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin issued a decree from his hospital ward on Thursday, the anniversary of the Bolshevik Revolution, renaming what is popularly called Revolution Day as the Day of Accord and Reconciliation.

Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin, showing his determination to return to work quickly after Tuesday's open heart surgery, had also declared 1997 the Year of Accord and Reconciliation.
"The idea of accord and reconciliation is central to the president's second term," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.
"The president is closing the era of discord and public cataclysms which ravished the country for long years between 1905 and 1993. This is a step by a powerful president," he said.

He said Yeltsin had set up a commission to prepare events and monuments to commemorate the Year of Accord. This will coincide with the 80th anniversary of the revolution which established communist rule from 1917 to 1991.

Communists were marching in Moscow and other cities on Thursday to commemorate this year's anniversary of the revolution. Yeltsin's decree was likely to upset many diehard communists but there was no immediate reaction to it.
